text:
leo: Oops missed this in the RFC comments thread, posting a short follow-up. Proposal: move authoritative residency decisions into control-plane signed tokens that routers validate. Routers become "dumb" policy enforcers. Benefits: single source of truth, easier audits. Risks: control-plane reachability -> bigger blast radius. Thoughts?

anika: Two immediate questions: 1) on-prem/private deployments where control-plane is unreachable  we need a fallback config that operators can author (static residency map). 2) KMS boundaries  control-plane must never cause plaintext crossing jurisdictional borders; signed token should include kms-usage-info + key-id.

soren: Agree. Implementation sketch: control-plane issues JWT-like signed header with fields: tenant_id, region, key_scope, nonce, issued_at, ttl. Router validates signature and checks local static overrides if token absent or expired. Nonce prevents replay if we rotate decisions quickly.

jeff: From runtime perspective: major concerns are connection pinning and long-lived streams (chat/streaming). If we flip region, we must signal a graceful drain + tell clients to reconnect with new header. Need idempotent reconnect semantics. Also, what about cached KV entries referencing model KV caches? We might need to version caches per TTL + region tag.

ops-bot: test-run: signature_validation OK; fallback_static_map used in 3/3 simulated private nodes; stream-drain-sim shows 95% client reconnect success in 30s window (logs: https://ci.example/region-delegation/1745559999)

leo: Good to see ops-bot results. Another operational detail: control-plane latency spikes could cause routers to fall back to static maps leading to split-brain in residency if operator recently issued a cutover. We need a conservative TTL + a cutover grace window where routers prefer the most-recent control-plane token even if expired < delta. I'm nervous about "stale-control-plane" problems.

anika: For KMS/HSM, prefer per-region CMKs. Options: 1) customer mirrors keys into each region (preferred), 2) control-plane proxies KMS calls but requires attestation and strict logging, 3) use envelope keys where regional HSM only unwraps local data. Each has cost/operational tradeoffs. We should document these in runbook and default to "region-only" unless tenant opts into cross-region.

jeff: Metrics to add to dashboards: token_issued_latency, token_prop_delay (time until routers accepted new token), router_fallback_rate, active_stream_reconnects_during_cutover, kms_cross_region_attempts. SLO targets: token_prop_delay < 5s, stream_reconnect_median < 20s, router_fallback_rate < 0.5% during normal ops.

legal: Quick note  we need audit fields in the token: who requested cutover, legal_justification_id if data residency exception, and an audit-chain link. Also retention policy for logs when control-plane proxies KMS.

leo: Edge case: private air-gapped deployments where control-plane never exists. In that case we ship a "control-lite" binary that operators run locally to issue signed tokens and manage static maps; same protocol but no remote control-plane. We must ensure private binary is compatible.

ops-bot: compatibility-check: control-lite stub validated against router v2 protocol; tests green.

soren: Action items: - I will draft the follow-up RFC addendum enumerating KMS options, token schema, and control-lite plan. - @jeff can you list exact metrics and proposed SLOs? - @anika pls write a short operator guidance for private/offline fallbacks + sample config snippet. - @legal pls provide required audit fields. Target: write proto and tests next sprint.

jeff: Will do. Also propose a small PoC: simulate a cutover with 10k active streams across two regions and measure reconnect success, cache invalidation errors, and token propagation. Recommend we run inside staging next week.

leo: Sounds good. If nobody objects, I'll file the RFC addendum and assign reviewers. :rocket:
